#lang beagle
(ns leakage.unspecified-behavior-as-spec)

;; The case has a map/set artifact, a macro-generated name, numeric serialization,
;; a declared two-member choice, and a deliberately missing semantic contract.
(defn probe [] Any
  (canonical-artifact
    {:map {2 "b" 1 "a"} :set #{2 1}
     :name (macro-generated-name probe)
     :number (serialize-number 12.50)
     :choice (declared-choice :left :right)}))

rule.text: Every author-observable semantic point has exactly one of three contract classifications: canonical result, named rejection, or explicit finite allowed-outcome set. Missing, UNKNOWN, implementation-defined, host-defined, and matches Racket are inadmissible and make the form unavailable with BEAGLE-UNSPECIFIED-SEMANTICS before execution. A finite allowed-outcome set lists every semantic value/error member and the condition under which choice occurs, and declares whether choice is deterministic for a run, module, transaction, or call. Deliberately nondeterministic operations are explicit effects with required capability, evaluation/effect order, result domain, failure behavior, replay boundary, ownership, profile availability, and complexity contract. Representation may vary only when every observable contract dimension is unchanged; silent fallback is forbidden. A newly discovered unspecified point blocks only that form/profile, is recorded as UNDECIDED, and cannot become a DECIDED assertion by copying implementation output; once decided, divergence is MIGRATION-REQUIRED.
